copy.blurb: Scotland arrive at 18% in our model but just 11% on Kalshi — a 7.3-point gap that marks the largest disagreement on the board. Brazil, the favourite everywhere, graded at 65% by our frame and 70% by the market, are priced tighter than their pre-tournament résumé might warrant. The source of the split is form: Scotland beat 10-man Curaçao in their final friendly and per BBC Sport, "head to World Cup in buoyant mood," while Brazil, despite squads of that quality, showed patchy qualification and per ESPN, won only 6-2 against Panama — not the scoreline of a team untroubled. The market has not yet fully repriced that recent weakness, and our model, which weights qualification and warm-up results directly, has. Gilmour's absence (a knee injury sustained against Curaçao, per The Guardian) is material to Scotland's chances, but it sits already inside the model's 18%, not outside it. The pick rests on the market's lag in adjusting to Brazil's early sharpness and Scotland's late momentum.

copy.squad_blurb: Billy Gilmour will miss the tournament with a knee injury sustained in Scotland's friendly against Curaçao, per The Guardian. Neymar carries a calf complaint heading into the match for Brazil, per ESPN.
copy.summary: Scotland trail the market by 7.3 points at 11%, while our model rates them at 18%. The gap widens because the market has leaned harder into Brazil's credentials than recent form justifies, even accounting for the Scots' squad losses.
